[ASSISTANT_SAID] A Pareto distribution is a right-skewed distribution that can be used to model income or wealth distributions. It is characterized by a shape parameter (α) and a scale parameter (k).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To model y with a Pareto distribution, you can generate a random sample of values from the Pareto distribution and use these values as inputs to the existing functions you have defined.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] MATLAB code provided to generate a random sample of values from the Pareto distribution:  
```matlab
% Define the parameters of the Pareto distribution
alpha = 2;
k = 1;

% Generate a random sample of values from the Pareto distribution
n = 1000; % number of samples
y = k * (1-rand(1,n)).^(-1/alpha);
```  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] You can then use the `y` values as inputs to your existing `eval_lambdas` and `eval_lambdat` functions to get the corresponding values of the cut-off values `lambda`.  
[USER] I would like also to have thresholds for every y. How should I change the code accordingly?  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In order to model y with a Pareto distribution, you will need to specify the parameters of the distribution, such as the shape parameter and the scale parameter.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To add a threshold for every y, you will need to modify the code to only generate y values that are above a certain threshold.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example MATLAB code provided to incorporate a threshold into the code:  
```matlab
% Generate random y values with a Pareto distribution
alpha = 2; % shape parameter
beta = 1; % scale parameter
threshold = 10; % threshold value

y = -1;
while y < threshold
    y = beta * random(makedist('Pareto', 'a', alpha));
end

% Use y in the rest of the code as needed
```
